approach.method_basis: The Parent runs one task-local graph-evolution loop. A Gaussian process is refitted to every accepted score using integer Morgan environment counts and generalized Tanimoto covariance. A score-ranked population supplies parents for connected-fragment crossover and short sequences of atom, bond and ring mutations, producing a fresh field of 160 valid, unseen molecules. Correlated posterior draws select the ten evaluations; after three non-improving batches, eligibility narrows to the forty highest predicted means until progress resumes. Accepted molecules update the global training archive and a greedy population of sixty-four survivors. Stable canonical identities, duplicate rejection and a generating-parent-relative sulfur rule guard proposals. Its most recent change removed an unexercised mutation-effort floor and reproduced the preceding trajectories exactly. Thus the reference already includes count-sensitive learning, stochastic allocation and stall-dependent eligibility, but it has one shared model and one breeding population, with no independently progressing regions or restart episodes.
approach.novelty: Replace that loop with two independently progressing graph-local Bayesian optimizers. Each has its own scored center, owned training records, local posterior, bounded edit-path neighborhood and progress counters. Their posterior samples compete in common raw-score units for all ten evaluations. Repeated progress expands a region; repeated failure contracts it, then retires its minimum-radius episode and restarts from a different molecule already scored in the session. This is one coupled controller replacement: local modeling, local proposal support and progress-driven restart operate together. There are no completed siblings on this exact Parent in the supplied brief. Earlier relatives changed a global response mixture or retained more diverse breeders; neither coupled separate regional posteriors to their own neighborhoods, observations and restarts. The parallel tree-search ticket learns credit over edit prefixes, whereas this method continues to learn predictive score distributions within regional episodes.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is prolonged exploitation of one evolving breeding lineage without a controller that can independently contract and abandon an unproductive local episode. Actual Parent n-cf8d309c06de summaries and run logs show all fifteen cells completed, 4,350 accepted optimizer proposals, no invalid/duplicate oracle proposals, seed macros 0.649701282562401, 0.585233817344553 and 0.586155848726439, and mean 0.607030316211131 (available-seed SD 0.030175277546149237). Independently reading all fifteen Parent trajectories gives only 253 strict global-incumbent improvements and total positive sequential increment mass 5.978073077532332; only 0.6504706051605506 falls in evaluations 211-300. The seed-1 zaleplon trajectory makes its last strict improvement at evaluation 97, leaving 203 accepted evaluations without further improvement. Source inspection confirms one full-archive GP, greedy64 survival, quantile breeding and a stall mask, rather than separate local models. The Parent analysis reports scaffold concentration and recent-parent dominance; these motivate the controller question, not a claim that the global predictor is universally inaccurate. Earlier n-c415372c2c82 changed 433/435 purchase sets but lost 0.05622021886844667 and enlarged the >50-heavy-atom tail; n-e1a97c9e8713 increased reachable skeleton diversity but reduced incumbent mass from 5.978073 to 5.269884. The global response mixture n-1c27fae8e61d lost 0.13664347597349566 while often discounting the incumbent's small component, and n-37a4fc183d94 exposed more niche breeders without useful endpoint conversion. These are counterexamples to diversity, split labels or purchase changes alone. They do not test region-owned models with raw-unit sample competition and progress-driven retirement. n-61b9b3bfb40d is used only where the supplied Parent evidence establishes exact trajectory equivalence; no other historical composition is treated as the code Parent.

adoptions.applicability: The Parent already implements accepted-only count-GP inference and correlated sampling, while its one global learner/breeder can stall for long periods. This adoption tests independent local control using the same actual task-local label channel and unchanged real evaluation budget.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Couple independent local probabilistic models to incumbent-centered regions and allocate a shared evaluation budget by competing Thompson samples across regions.

adoptions.implementation_change: Construct each fresh candidate by a recorded center-rooted sequence of inherited molecular transformations and couple its regional posterior/controller state to real descendant feedback and restart.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen w4-graph-search-controller-review and its recorded queries/source findings; no new search or review-less source node is claimed. Adopt the local-model/region/Thompson-allocation/controller/reset coupling and explicitly adapt its geometry, initialization, counter horizon and restart support to the actual code Parent. Internal evidence motivates the specific bottleneck, not the source papers reported scores. The failed global mixture and niche retention arms reject simpler analogies, so the registered mechanism requires separate owned fits, graph paths, raw-unit competition and observed post-contraction/restart use. This is neither a reproduction of TuRBO/CASMOPOLITAN nor LOL-BO, and it introduces no pretrained asset or dependency.

method_change.previous_method: One full accepted-archive count-GP guiding score-quantile graph breeding, greedy64 retention and a three-batch-stall top-forty posterior-mean eligibility mask.
method_change.proposed_method: Two episode-owned count-GPs over separately initialized graph regions, raw-score Thompson competition, successful-edit-path neighborhoods, accepted-progress radius adaptation and scored-center restart.
method_change.rationale: The actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de has no independent local progress/retirement controller; its measured long late-session nonprogress, together with unsuccessful global mixture and diversity-only relatives, supports testing this distinct coupled unit. Count features and stochastic acquisition remain locally, but global breeder membership, one shared fit, the old path-length/finishing law and the global stall mask are necessarily replaced as one coherent method. The result identifies the replacement jointly and grants no contribution credit to retained or removed components.

hypothesis: Two-region graph-local posterior control with observed-progress contraction and restart. The coupled unit is (region, episode): a scored incumbent, a task-local seed set and accepted descendant labels, an independently conditioned count-GP, a finite successful-edit-path radius and counters updated solely by that episode's real accepted purchases. Each field contains region-labeled descendants of the two current centers. Independent local joint function draws are restored to raw objective units, concatenated and competed for the entire announced oracle batch, without regional purchase quotas or a global posterior-mean stall mask. A region with repeated measured failure contracts; repeated failure at minimum extent retires its episode and resets its local fit at a different already scored task-local center. Regional ownership, local support and reset are causally coupled, not a mixture average over one global pool. The intended path is separate local fits -> region-dependent raw sample prices and purchased descendants -> feedback-dependent extent and restart -> useful local progress after contraction/restart -> potentially more global incumbent increment per actual evaluation. It does not assume that graph-path radius is graph edit distance or that additional scaffolds alone improve the score.

finding_summary.headline: Local fits and restarts ran, but useful improvement per evaluation fell 8.94%
finding_summary.insights:
Independent models and working restarts were insufficient to sustain useful competition between regions. Both regions received labels in ten sessions, but 406 of 435 batches bought from only one region. Two restarted regions spent 42 later fits and 3,360 proposals with one training label, scale 0.001 and no purchases; the correct no-purchase rule then left their state unchanged. This identifies a limitation in cross-region uncertainty calibration and feedback exposure. A model that compares uncertainty across very different local data sizes, or a search scheme that can replace unexposed regions, is the kind of methodological change that could address it; these data do not show which would improve scores.

The molecular evidence also separates field variety from useful accepted exploration. Generated-field similarity fell from 0.60468 to 0.49733, while purchased-molecule similarity rose from 0.71338 to 0.75259. Small-fragment purchases increased from 91 to 133 and produced no global gain; purchases above fifty heavy atoms increased from 44 to 284 and contributed only 0.04083 total global improvement. Repeated aromatic/carbonyl and fluorinated heterocyclic families still dominate successful structures, with reactive heteroatom caps and unspecified stereochemistry. A construction method that preserves coherent alternative cores is relevant to that limitation, but chemical plausibility is not demonstrated to improve this benchmark.

The three borrowed local-model, adaptive-neighborhood and restart elements operated in their declared graph adaptations. Their continuous or categorical guarantees do not transfer: one successful graph step can change size substantially, and reset initialization has only one known label. The result settles the frozen joint configuration’s claim of better budget conversion. It does not isolate the contributions of local fitting, removing the old mask, graph construction or restart, nor end the broader local-optimization approach. The total global-increment mass telescopes to endpoint improvement from the common initial best, so it is not an independent causal proof of why the score changed.
finding_summary.results: The construction and control checks passed across all fifteen sessions: 870 separate local fits replaced 435 global fits, all 4,350 purchases matched the raw-score sample auction, and the controller made 38 contractions, 16 expansions and 15 actual restarts. Thirteen restarted episodes received purchases and nine improved their local and global incumbents. Across 850 post-restart purchases, local improvement totaled 0.19539 and global improvement 0.14911. Yet the complete panel produced more, smaller global improvements: 278 versus 253, with total improvement falling from 5.97807 to 5.44337 over the same 4,350 optimizer evaluations. Improvement per evaluation fell from 0.00137427 to 0.00125135, triggering the registered useful-conversion falsifier. Mean endpoint score fell from 0.60703 to 0.57138, a paired change of -0.03565; one seed improved and two declined. Gains on zaleplon, median_2 and the drd2 mean did not offset losses on deco_hop and sitagliptin. This is an executed mechanism with a refuted conversion claim, not a technical failure or merely a missed endpoint threshold.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic output includes coherent small scaffolds, but also reactive heteroatom caps, size extremes and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Scope: n-bc1f80092068 compared descriptively with its published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, Research in Depth epoch 1, Search seeds 0/1/2, all five objectives, 300 observations per cell including ten initial records and batches of ten. context.comparison reports both child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; all 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory paths and their task logs exist and were read. No task, seed or Parent pairing is absent. The evidence is the immutable request policy/requests/r0050-01-improve-L01-molecular-assess-176cc005f028fa76.json, its exact focus.artifacts.this_node_trajectories and parent_trajectories files, and each corresponding Search task log. Complete derived per-cell descriptors, full heavy-atom distributions, high/low observed-score strata, exact representative structures and source file paths are in policy/scratch/r0050-01-molecular/population.json; generalized count-similarity recomputation is in policy/scratch/r0050-01-molecular/similarities.json. Scripts there perform offline structure analysis only. Citation authority remains the request digest and context.citation_trajectory_paths, not these derived files. Each panel contributes 4,500 trajectory rows, comprising 150 initial and 4,350 optimizer records, plus 69,600 admitted generated-field occurrences over 435 batches. All 4,350 optimizer records and all 69,600 field occurrences parse with RDKit in each panel. Field counts are occurrences, including recurrence across batches, not unique molecules or new oracle evaluations. Rejected construction retries and intermediate path states are not admitted-field molecules; their controller meaning is outside this report. Scores are read only for actual trajectory records. No unpurchased field molecule receives an inferred score. Child accepted heavy atoms range 1-120, median 30, versus Parent 1-96, median 28. Child accepted lower/upper size tails are 133 below six and 284 above fifty, versus Parent 91 and 44. Child full-field tails are 2,661 and 6,852, versus Parent 2,130 and 2,776. All Child below-six purchases have zero strict global-incumbent increment; above-fifty purchases make 25 increments totaling 0.04082757883773969. These are chronological observed increments from the initial incumbent, not causal credit or counterfactual benefits of excluding a molecule. Ring and aromatic content are genuinely abundant in the accepted structures: 4,206/4,350 have perceived rings and 4,181/4,350 have aromatic atoms. This agrees with digest SMILES ring-closure rates 0.9506-0.9759 and aromatic-token rates 0.9483-0.9690. Full fields have 66,392 ring-bearing and 59,302 aromatic-bearing occurrences; accepted aromatic enrichment cannot be projected onto every unscored proposal. Child accepted nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 1,717/1,047 versus Parent 1,667/951; corresponding full-field counts are 20,351/12,632 versus Parent 23,723/12,517. Distinct canonical Child identities are 4,301 accepted and 49,046 field, versus Parent 4,304 and 61,719. These structural counters do not measure synthetic accessibility. Across all 435 batches per panel, after excluding molecules below six heavy atoms, mean within-batch generalized count-Morgan Tanimoto is Child field 0.4973273593364688 versus Parent 0.604676980961103, and Child accepted 0.7525858973354357 versus Parent 0.7133792182993748. All batches retain at least two molecules, so none is undefined. Radius-2, 2,048-bin chirality-aware integer Morgan vectors use dot/(squared_norm_1+squared_norm_2-dot), not sparse-integer min/max Tanimoto. Independent recomputation matches all 870 Child logged field/accepted molecular similarity receipts within 6.22e-15. Thus chemically varied fields coexist with concentrated accepted families; this association does not attribute a component effect. Specific liabilities are pervasive: 1,228 accepted structures have N-halogen bonds, 336 O-halogen, 32 S-halogen, five halogen-halogen, and 166 peroxide motifs; categories overlap and identify connectivity, not proven decomposition. There are also 577 N-S-containing structures; this broad count includes ordinary sulfonamides and is not itself a liability, whereas unusual sulfur capping is identified in the representative molecules. Parent accepted N-halogen/O-halogen counts are 888/162. RDKit identifies possible stereocentres in 2,352 Child accepted molecules, but none has a specified atom stereocentre; field counts are 38,966 possible-centre-bearing occurrences and zero specified. No accepted molecule has a formal charge; this does not mean none can ionize. The quality chips summarize this mixture: extensive rings and aromatics, moderate whole-population structural variety, but weak conventional medicinal plausibility and questionable synthesis because of unusual bond roles, extreme sizes and unspecified stereochemistry. Some individual products are plausible organic compounds; no reaction planning, experimental stability or biological validation is provided. Per-task high/low strata use the top and bottom 29 existing optimizer scores within each seed, with evaluation-order tie breaking, and contain 87 records each. They are descriptive selections of measured molecules; neither task requirements nor improvements to an optimizer are inferred from objective names. No activation verdict, ranking of algorithms, hidden-task guidance, held-out evidence or component attribution is made.

per_task.generated_character: Complete population: each of seeds 0/1/2 contributes 290 optimizer records and 4,640 admitted field occurrences, after ten initial records; all parse with RDKit. Accepted heavy atoms range 1-51, median 25; 33/870 are below six and 3/870 above fifty. These accepted lower/upper tail counts by seed are [(11, 1), (10, 0), (12, 2)]. The complete unscored field ranges 1-81, median 26, with 305/13920 below six and 301/13920 above fifty. Accepted molecules with rings/aromatic atoms are 836/835 of 870; median perceived rings/aromatic rings are 3/3. Accepted nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 258/106, versus Parent 186/69; field counts are 3217/1576, versus Parent 3026/1328. Parent accepted size median is 25, lower/upper tails 20/0. Fragment-excluded mean within-batch generalized count-Tanimoto is field 0.496969, accepted 0.720888; corresponding Parent values 0.576202/0.705678. The accepted chemistry is concentrated on substituted indole-like fused aromatic cores with a second aryl or pyridyl group, carbonyl linkers, methoxy/alkyl substitution and occasional nitrile. The seed-1 champion has 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings: an N-methylindole-like core bearing nitrile and methoxy groups, linked through a ketone/methylene unit to pyridine. It is a comparatively coherent small organic structure. Seed-0 and seed-2 champions retain similar aromatic/carbonyl assemblies but carry N-S bonds; seed 2 also has an N-Cl amide and extra ring closure. These make the complete output less conventionally plausible than the cleanest example alone suggests.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 188/870 accepted molecules and N-S attachment appears in the cited seed-0 and seed-2 champions; valence-valid representations do not establish stability or practical synthesis.
The accepted lower tail contains 33 tiny fragments and the upper tail three molecules above fifty heavy atoms; neither tail contributes a strict incumbent increment in this task.
Predominantly aromatic, closely related top families limit the evidence for diverse chemically coherent solutions; no experimental synthesis or biological assessment is supplied.
missing_features: Reliable access to similarly compact aromatic/carbonyl alternatives without reactive heteroatom capping is incomplete: one seed finds such a structure, while the other champions retain N-S or N-Cl bonds. This is a consistency gap, not absence of aromatic rings, nitriles, amides or heterocycles.
Only eight generic scaffolds occur in the 87 top-stratum records. The trajectories do not establish a unique absent pharmacophore or that further ring growth would be rewarded.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Observed best scores for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.460926, 0.542326, 0.458807; published Parent values are 0.423482, 0.438799, 0.450504. The seed-1 champion scores 0.5423261445466404, compared with the shared best initial indole carboxamide at 0.3051048083696145. Across the top observed-score tenth within each seed (29 records per seed; 87 total), heavy atoms lie between 23 and 26, median 25, and every molecule retains rings and aromatic atoms. In the bottom tenth, median heavy atoms is 10, with 33 below six. The cited SCl and C=COS both score zero. The association favors retention of a connected aromatic/carbonyl assembly at moderate size, rather than arbitrary atom addition; the nitrile/ketone substitution is a successful observed example, not an independently identified necessary group. Late seed-2 molecules still vary in score, so the last proposal is not the best molecule.

The seed-0 champion has 37 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings with an amide, alkoxy groups, imine and hydrazine-like N-N linkage. Ring chemistry is abundant, but the combination of duplicated decoration, unusual heteroatom bonds and large tails makes synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: N-halogen and O-halogen bonds occur in 287 and 214 of 870 accepted molecules, respectively; these categories overlap. N-F, N-Cl and O-Br are present together in the quoted best seed-1 molecule.

There are 242 accepted molecules above fifty heavy atoms, including 179 in seed 0, and the maximum is 120. The upper tail does make 24 strict incumbent increments with total mass 0.03092266434418578, so it cannot be dismissed as universally score-useless; nevertheless all three final best molecules are below fifty heavy atoms.

Amidine/acetal-like joining, reactive halogen capping, N-N attachment and numerous altered ring/linker combinations provide no demonstrated synthesis route. The 22 accepted below-six fragments make no incumbent increment.
missing_features: Consistent exploration of compact alternative N-heterocyclic and linker arrangements is missing from the successful end of this trajectory: extended and repeatedly decorated structures dominate much of the accepted population. The Parent example shows that large size is not necessary in the observed comparison.

No single missing decoration or target-like motif can be inferred from the floor and near-tied top variants. The output lacks a demonstrated route to higher observed scores through coherent core replacement, rather than decoration multiplication.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Observed best scores for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.607960, 0.610727, 0.605566; published Parent values are 0.856148, 0.621729, 0.644234. The cited O=CCF and NCl both score 0.5, the observed floor; that value is not evidence that these fragments meet a meaningful chemical objective. The 87 top-stratum records are 34-48 heavy atoms with median 39; the bottom tenth has median 23, including 22 below six, but also reaches 79 heavy atoms. The best seed-1 score is 0.610726643598616 and several different linkage/capping variants share it. Merely adding size or rings is therefore not a sufficient reading of this gradient. The published Parent seed-0 best reaches 0.8561477222467935 with a more compact 30-heavy-atom, five-ring N-heterocyclic structure, but it also contains an O-F bond: the comparison does not identify chemical stability as the rewarded property.

liabilities: The seed-2 champion carries an N-Cl group and a thiophenol. The seed-0 champion combines a small saturated N ring, chlorinated stereogenic carbons and a sulfoxide; its five RDKit-perceived possible stereocentres are unspecified.
N-halogen bonds occur in 139/870 accepted molecules. Neutral SMILES do not determine protonation state or amine basicity, and no formal charge is specified in any accepted structure.

Twenty accepted molecules have fewer than six heavy atoms and make no incumbent increment. Twenty-three exceed fifty heavy atoms, with one strict increment of 0.009904914493553914; the three best molecules remain much smaller.
missing_features: The generator already supplies ionizable-looking saturated amines and aromatic partners. What it does not supply consistently is that combination with chemically conservative substituents and specified stereochemistry.

No additional absent binding motif is supported by these near-ceiling observed scores. The missing evidence is whether the same chemical pattern remains successful in coherent alternative scaffolds without N-halogen attachment or strained ring/linker construction.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
